topics.title: Harsha and the struggle for Kannauj

learn.hook: For about two hundred years, three powerful dynasties fought again and again over one city: Kannauj!
points: After the Guptas declined, many regional kingdoms rose across India between the 6th and 10th centuries.
Harṣhavardhana (Harsha) ruled from 606 to 647 CE, first from Thanesar and then from Kannauj. His court poet Bāṇabhaṭṭa wrote his life story, the Harṣhacharita. Harsha himself wrote Sanskrit plays.
The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) visited India in Harsha's time and studied at Nālandā.
After Harsha, Kannauj on the Ganga became a prize city. The Gurjara-Pratīhāras, the Pālas and the Rāṣhṭrakūṭas fought for it; historians call this the Tripartite Struggle ('three-sided struggle').
The Pālas ruled Bengal and Bihar. Gopāla, the first Pāla king, is said to have been chosen by local chiefs. Dharmapāla founded the Buddhist university of Vikramashilā.

example.q: Why did three distant dynasties all want to control Kannauj?
steps: Kannauj stood on the Ganga in the fertile plains, with rich farmland and trade.
Since Harsha's time it was seen as the most important city of north India.
Controlling it brought wealth and great prestige.
example.answer: Because Kannauj was wealthy, on important routes, and a symbol of power in north India.

learn.reallife: Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh is now famous for making attar (natural perfume), but it was once the capital that every empire wanted.

games.title: Who's who?
pairs: King who ruled from Kannauj, 606–647 CE
Chinese pilgrim who studied at Nālandā
First Pāla king, chosen by chiefs

quiz.q: Harṣhavardhana's capital for most of his reign was:
quiz.explain: Harsha moved from Thanesar to Kannauj, which became his capital.
quiz.mistake: Picks a capital of another dynasty

quiz.q: Who wrote the Harṣhacharita?
quiz.explain: Bāṇabhaṭṭa, Harsha's court poet, wrote his biography.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous authors

quiz.q: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India during Harsha's reign?
quiz.explain: Xuanzang came in the 7th century and studied at Nālandā. Faxian came earlier, in the Gupta age.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Xuanzang with Faxian

quiz.q: The Tripartite Struggle was fought for control of:
quiz.explain: The three powers fought over Kannauj in the Ganga plains.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Delhi was already the main capital

quiz.q: Which three dynasties fought the Tripartite Struggle?
quiz.explain: These three powers from the north-west, east and Deccan competed for Kannauj.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up dynasties of different periods

quiz.q: The Pāla dynasty ruled mainly in:
quiz.explain: The Pālas ruled the eastern region of Bengal and Bihar.
quiz.mistake: Does not place the Pālas on the map

quiz.q: Who founded the university of Vikramashilā?
quiz.explain: The Pāla king Dharmapāla founded Vikramashilā.
quiz.mistake: Credits another famous ruler

quiz.q: What does 'tripartite' mean?
quiz.explain: 'Tri' means three; three powers took part.
quiz.mistake: Does not break the word into parts

teach.ask: Gappu asks who ruled north India after the Guptas, and why Kannauj was so important.
teach.praise: Harsha ruled from Kannauj, and then three dynasties fought over it. A city worth fighting for!
teach.nudge: Good! Which three powers fought over Kannauj after Harsha?

learn.hook: In the 7th century, two southern kingdoms competed fiercely but also created some of India's most beautiful temples.
points: The Chālukyas of Bādāmi (Vātāpi) ruled much of the Deccan in present-day Karnataka. Their greatest king, Pulakeshin II, stopped Harsha's advance at the Narmada river.
Pulakeshin II's victories are recorded in the Aihole inscription, composed by his court poet Ravikīrti.
The Pallavas ruled from Kānchīpuram in present-day Tamil Nadu. Mahendravarman I was a king and a playwright. His son Narasiṁhavarman I, called Māmalla, captured Vātāpi in 642 CE.

The port town of Māmallapuram (Mahabalipuram) is named after Māmalla. It has the Pañcha Rathas (temples cut from single rocks), the great rock relief often called Arjuna's Penance, and the Shore Temple.
The Chālukyas built fine temples at Aihole, Bādāmi and Pattadakal. The temples at Pattadakal and the monuments at Mahabalipuram are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

example.q: Two kingdoms were rivals and fought many wars, yet both built magnificent temples. What does this tell us about the period?
steps: Kings showed their power through victories and through grand buildings.
They supported architects, sculptors and poets.
So even in times of war, art and architecture flourished.
example.answer: That rulers competed not only in war but also in art and temple-building, so culture flourished.

learn.reallife: The Shore Temple and the Pañcha Rathas at Mahabalipuram, near Chennai, attract visitors from all over the world.

quiz.q: The capital of the Chālukyas of Bādāmi was:
quiz.explain: Vātāpi, today's Bādāmi in Karnataka, was the Chālukya capital.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Chālukya and Pallava capitals

quiz.q: Which Chālukya king stopped Harsha at the Narmada?
quiz.explain: Pulakeshin II defeated Harsha's attempt to move south.
quiz.mistake: Picks a king of another dynasty

quiz.q: The Aihole inscription was composed by:
quiz.explain: Ravikīrti, Pulakeshin II's court poet, composed it.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with Samudragupta's praśasti by Hariṣheṇa

quiz.q: The Pallavas ruled from:
quiz.explain: Kānchīpuram in Tamil Nadu was the Pallava capital.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Pallavas with the later Cholas

quiz.q: Narasiṁhavarman I, who captured Vātāpi in 642 CE, was also called:
quiz.explain: He was called Māmalla, 'great wrestler'; Māmallapuram is named after him.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up royal titles

quiz.q: The Pañcha Rathas at Mahabalipuram are:
options: Temples cut out of single rocks
quiz.explain: Each ratha is carved from one large rock, in the shape of a temple.
quiz.mistake: Takes 'ratha' to mean a real chariot

quiz.q: Pattadakal, with its group of temples, was built by the:
quiz.explain: The Chālukyas built the Pattadakal temples in Karnataka.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Chālukya and Pallava monuments

quiz.q: Mahendravarman I was not only a king but also a:
quiz.explain: He wrote Sanskrit plays.
quiz.mistake: Confuses him with other famous figures

teach.ask: Gappu wants to visit the south. Tell him about the Chālukyas and Pallavas and what they built.
teach.praise: Rival kingdoms who both built amazing temples! I'll visit Bādāmi and Mahabalipuram.
teach.nudge: Good! Which temples did each dynasty build?

learn.hook: Imagine carving a whole temple, top to bottom, out of a single mountain of rock. The Rāṣhṭrakūṭas did it at Ellora!
points: The Rāṣhṭrakūṭas rose in the Deccan in the 8th century when Dantidurga overthrew the Chālukyas of Bādāmi. Their later capital was Mānyakheṭa.
King Kṛiṣhṇa I had the Kailāsa temple at Ellora carved from a single rock, from the top downwards. It is one of the largest rock-cut monuments in the world.
King Amoghavarṣha I supported literature; the Kavirājamārga, an early work on Kannada poetry, was written in his court.
In this period, the Ālvārs (devotees of Vishnu) and Nāyanārs (devotees of Shiva) composed devotional songs in Tamil, spreading bhakti, or loving devotion.
Great universities like Nālandā and Vikramashilā drew students from many lands. In 712 CE, Arab forces under Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh, bringing new contacts with West Asia.

example.q: Carving the Kailāsa temple began at the top of the rock and went downwards. Why might sculptors carve from the top?
steps: When you remove rock from the top, it falls away without damaging the parts below.
Workers could stand on the uncut rock as a platform.
This avoided the need for tall scaffolding.
example.answer: Carving from the top let rock fall away safely and gave workers a place to stand, without scaffolding.

learn.reallife: The Ellora caves near Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) have Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves side by side: a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

games.title: Rāṣhṭrakūṭas and culture
items: The Kailāsa temple at Ellora was carved from a single rock.
It was cut downwards out of one huge rock.
The Kavirājamārga is an early work on Kannada poetry.
It was written in Amoghavarṣha I's court.
The Ālvārs were devotees of Shiva.
The Ālvārs were devotees of Vishnu; the Nāyanārs were devotees of Shiva.
Ellora has Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.
They ruled in the Deccan; their later capital was Mānyakheṭa.

quiz.q: Who founded the power of the Rāṣhṭrakūṭas?
quiz.explain: Dantidurga overthrew the Chālukyas of Bādāmi in the 8th century.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up founders of different dynasties

quiz.q: The Kailāsa temple at Ellora was built under:
quiz.explain: The Rāṣhṭrakūṭa king Kṛiṣhṇa I had it carved.
quiz.mistake: Credits the wrong dynasty

quiz.q: What is special about the Kailāsa temple?
options: It was carved from a single rock
It was built of bricks in one day
quiz.explain: It is a monolithic temple, cut out of one huge rock.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what rock-cut means

quiz.q: The Kavirājamārga is an early work in which language?
quiz.explain: It is an early Kannada work on poetics, from Amoghavarṣha I's court.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up southern languages

quiz.q: The Ālvārs and Nāyanārs composed devotional songs in:
quiz.explain: Their bhakti songs were composed in Tamil.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where they lived

quiz.q: The Nāyanārs were devotees of:
quiz.explain: Nāyanārs worshipped Shiva; Ālvārs worshipped Vishnu.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two groups of saints

quiz.q: In 712 CE, Sindh was conquered by Arab forces led by:
quiz.explain: Muhammad bin Qasim led the Arab conquest of Sindh in 712 CE.
quiz.mistake: Confuses him with later invaders

quiz.q: Which was the later capital of the Rāṣhṭrakūṭas?
quiz.explain: Mānyakheṭa (Malkhed in Karnataka) was their later capital.
quiz.mistake: Picks a capital of another dynasty

teach.ask: Gappu heard about a temple carved from a mountain. Tell him about the Rāṣhṭrakūṭas and the culture of this age.
teach.praise: A temple carved from a single rock, Kannada poetry and bhakti songs! What a creative time!
teach.nudge: Good! What did the Rāṣhṭrakūṭas build at Ellora?
